#### Normalize matrix by nanoseq coverage
```{r signaturesNormalize}

#Read in trinuc counts and ratio to full genome
backgroundRates <- read_tsv("<hpc_scratch>/sperm/germanTrio_data/postNextflow/signatures/trinucCounts.tsv", col_types = cols(), col_names = c("trinuc", "trinucCount", "ratio2genome", "Sample_PD_ID")) 
  
#Get mutation matrix generated by sigprofiler and then correct for ratio to genome
matrixNorm <- read_tsv("<hpc_scratch>/sperm/germanTrio_data/postNextflow/signatures/sigprofiler_in/output/SBS/sigprofiler_in.SBS96.all", col_types = cols()) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("PD"), names_to = "Sample_PD_ID", values_to = "mutCount") |> 
  mutate(trinuc = paste0(str_sub(MutationType, 1,1), str_sub(MutationType, 3,3),str_sub(MutationType, 7,7))) |> 
  left_join(backgroundRates, by = c("Sample_PD_ID", "trinuc")) |> 
  mutate(normCount = round(mutCount * 1/ratio2genome)) |> 
  select(MutationType, Sample_PD_ID,normCount) |> drop_na() |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = Sample_PD_ID, values_from = normCount) 

write_tsv(matrixNorm, "<hpc_scratch>/sperm/germanTrio_data/postNextflow/signatures/sigprofiler_in/output/SBS/sigprofiler_in.SBS96.normalized", col_names = T)

# Get normalized for all samples combined due to low mutation count per sample
matrixNormCombined <- read_tsv("<hpc_scratch>/sperm/germanTrio_data/postNextflow/signatures/sigprofiler_in/output/SBS/sigprofiler_in.SBS96.all", col_types = cols())|> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("PD"), names_to = "Sample_PD_ID", values_to = "mutCount") |> 
  mutate(trinuc = paste0(str_sub(MutationType, 1,1), str_sub(MutationType, 3,3),str_sub(MutationType, 7,7))) |> 
  left_join(backgroundRates, by = c("Sample_PD_ID", "trinuc")) |> 
  mutate(normCount = mutCount * 1/ratio2genome) |> 
  select(MutationType, Sample_PD_ID,normCount) |> drop_na() |> 
  mutate(dataset = if_else(str_detect(Sample_PD_ID, "PD5"), "Oxford", "GermanTrio")) |> 
  group_by(MutationType) |> 
summarize(
  Oxford = round(sum(normCount[dataset == "Oxford"], na.rm = TRUE)),
  GermanTrio = round(sum(normCount[dataset == "GermanTrio"], na.rm = TRUE)),
  .groups = "drop"
)

write_tsv(matrixNormCombined, "<hpc_scratch>/sperm/germanTrio_data/postNextflow/signatures/sigprofiler_in/output/SBS/sigprofiler_in.SBS96.normalized.combined", col_names = T)


```

## f) TwinsUK model fits (for public code fallback)
TwinsUK individual-level VAF sums (tukVafSums etc.) are under TwinsUK's controlled-access
policy and can't be shared publicly (see README in PublicCode/). The age-trend models
fitted on them are pure aggregate summaries (an Age grid + fitted value + 95% CI, or a
handful of scalar stats) with no way to recover individual data points, so those are
safe to export and let the public figures code draw the TwinsUK trend line/reported
stats without needing the underlying samples.

### Basic burdens
```{r targBurden, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
 
burdenTwinsUKTarg <- read_tsv(paste0("<local_working_dir>/nanoseqTwinsUK_Targ/data/burdensFiltered.tsv"), col_types = cols()) |>
  left_join(read_tsv(paste0("<local_working_dir>/nanoSampleMeta/targetedSamplesFiltered.tsv"), col_types = cols()), by = "Sample_PD_ID") |>
  mutate(nanoseq = "Controls") |>
  rename(Age = age_at_sampling) |> drop_na(Age)

# TwinsUK burden data is individual-level and controlled-access (see the
# "TwinsUK model fits" note in ## d) Observed VAFs). Save the age-trend fits
# only (aggregate Age grid + fit + CI, using the same age_grid_fine/fit_lm_grid
# helpers defined there) so the public figures code can draw the TwinsUK trend
# line without the underlying samples.
twinsUK_burdenFits <- bind_rows(
  fit_lm_grid(lm(burdenCorr ~ Age, data = burdenTwinsUKTarg)) |> mutate(model = "burdenCorr"),
  fit_lm_grid(lm(indelBurden ~ Age, data = burdenTwinsUKTarg)) |> mutate(model = "indelBurden")
)
write_tsv(twinsUK_burdenFits, paste0(localPath, "data/twinsUK_burdenFits.tsv"))

burdenCombined <- germanTrioBurdens |>
  mutate(burdenCorr = burdenCorr1percent, indelBurden = burdenIndelPost1percent) |> 
  mutate(nanoseq = if_else(str_detect(Sample_PD_ID, "PD5"),"Apert fathers", "DD fathers")) |> 
  bind_rows(burdenTwinsUKTarg) 

p_germanTrioBurdens <- ggplot(burdenCombined, aes(x = Age, y = burdenCorr, fill = nanoseq)) + 
  geom_point(size=3.5, pch=21, col='white', stroke=0.25) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_colours) +
   theme(text = element_text(size=16)) + 
  xlab('Age (years)') + 
  ylab('Mutations per bp') + 
  labs(fill='Dataset') + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  ylim(0,NA) 

p_germanTrioBurdens

p_indelBurden<- ggplot(burdenCombined, aes(x = Age, y = indelBurden, fill = nanoseq)) + 
  geom_point(size=3.5, pch=21, col='white', stroke=0.25) + 
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(1, 1, 0.8), guide = "none") + 
   theme(text = element_text(size=16)) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = dataset_colours) +
```

### VafSums
```{r twinsUKVafFits}
# Wider than the observed TwinsUK age range so ages back-inferred to conception
# (Age - paternalAgeGap) on the public side stay within the saved grid.
age_grid_fine <- tibble(Age = seq(10, 80, by = 1))

# Predict a model over the age grid with 95% CI - works for any simple lm(y ~ Age).
# Linear interpolation between grid points reproduces predict() exactly for a
# straight-line model, so this same grid also supports point predictions at
# arbitrary (non-grid) ages downstream via approx().
fit_lm_grid <- function(model, ages = age_grid_fine$Age) {
  pred <- predict(model, newdata = tibble(Age = ages), se.fit = TRUE, interval = "confidence", level = 0.95)
  tibble(Age = ages, fit = pred$fit[,"fit"], ci_lo = pred$fit[,"lwr"], ci_hi = pred$fit[,"upr"])
}

twins_model <- lm(exome_vafSum ~ Age, data = tukVafSums |> filter(vafGroup == "ClinDDlofCADD"))
twins_model_panel <- lm(vafSum ~ Age, data = tukVafSums |> filter(vafGroup == "ClinDDlofCADD"))
twins_model_driver <- lm(vafSum ~ Age, data = tukVafSums |> filter(vafGroup == "posPath"))
model_exome_posPath <- tukVafSums |> filter(vafGroup == "posPath") |> lm(exome_vafSum ~ Age, data = _)

# Quasibinomial smooth (used for the driver-rate panels) is not a simple lm, so the
# grid is predicted on the link scale then back-transformed, matching what
# stat_smooth(method = "glm", family = "quasibinomial") does internally.
fitQB_allPos <- glm(vafSum ~ Age, family = quasibinomial, data = tukVafSums |> filter(vafGroup == "allPos"))
predsQB <- predict(fitQB_allPos, newdata = age_grid_fine, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
gridQB <- tibble(
  Age = age_grid_fine$Age,
  fit = plogis(predsQB$fit),
  ci_lo = plogis(predsQB$fit - 1.96 * predsQB$se.fit),
  ci_hi = plogis(predsQB$fit + 1.96 * predsQB$se.fit)
) |> mutate(model = "vafSum_allPos_quasibinom")

# Note: "ClinDDlofCADD" is the internal vafGroup label from generate_vaf_summary();
# it's the same selection as what the public figures code calls "likelyDisease",
# so the saved model names use that more readable label instead.
twinsUK_vafFits <- bind_rows(
  fit_lm_grid(twins_model) |> mutate(model = "exome_vafSum_likelyDisease"),
  fit_lm_grid(twins_model_panel) |> mutate(model = "vafSum_likelyDisease"),
  fit_lm_grid(twins_model_driver) |> mutate(model = "vafSum_posPath"),
  fit_lm_grid(model_exome_posPath) |> mutate(model = "exome_vafSum_posPath"),
  gridQB
)
write_tsv(twinsUK_vafFits, paste0(localPath, "data/twinsUK_vafFits.tsv"))

# Exome-to-panel capture fraction: a single scalar plus reporting stats, all
# aggregate (see "Calibrate exome correction" in the public/DD-father section
# for how this constant is used).
fractionWithinPanel <- tukVafSums |>
  group_by(vafGroup) |>
  summarize(totalVAFs = sum(vafSum, na.rm = TRUE), totalVAFsExome = sum(exome_vafSum, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(percentageInPanel = totalVAFs / totalVAFsExome)
exomePanelCorrection <- fractionWithinPanel |> filter(vafGroup == "ClinDDlofCADD") |> pull(percentageInPanel)

panel_exome_df <- tukVafSums |>
  filter(vafGroup == "ClinDDlofCADD") |>
  mutate(percentageInPanel = vafSum / exome_vafSum) |>
  filter(is.finite(percentageInPanel), percentageInPanel > 0)

cor_test <- cor.test(panel_exome_df$vafSum, panel_exome_df$exome_vafSum, method = "pearson")
fit_age <- lm(percentageInPanel ~ Age, data = panel_exome_df)
fit_age_sum <- summary(fit_age)

twinsUK_exomePanelCorrection_stats <- tibble(
  exomePanelCorrection = exomePanelCorrection,
  n_samples = nrow(panel_exome_df),
  n_sources = dplyr::n_distinct(panel_exome_df$source),
  cor_estimate = unname(cor_test$estimate),
  cor_p_value = cor_test$p.value,
  age_beta_per_year = coef(fit_age)["Age"],
  age_se = coef(fit_age_sum)["Age", "Std. Error"],
  age_p_value = coef(fit_age_sum)["Age", "Pr(>|t|)"],
  age_r_squared = fit_age_sum$r.squared,
  mean_frac = mean(panel_exome_df$percentageInPanel, na.rm = TRUE),
  median_frac = median(panel_exome_df$percentageInPanel, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd_frac = sd(panel_exome_df$percentageInPanel, na.rm = TRUE),
  iqr_frac = IQR(panel_exome_df$percentageInPanel, na.rm = TRUE)
)
write_tsv(twinsUK_exomePanelCorrection_stats, paste0(localPath, "data/twinsUK_exomePanelCorrection_stats.tsv"))

twinsUK_vafFits <- bind_rows(twinsUK_vafFits, fit_lm_grid(fit_age) |> mutate(model = "percentageInPanel_exomeCorrection"))
write_tsv(twinsUK_vafFits, paste0(localPath, "data/twinsUK_vafFits.tsv"))
```

```{r supTable6}
  full_join(read_tsv("<local_working_dir>/genePanel/GermlinePanelV1/germlineV1_hg19.bed", col_types = 'cii--', col_names= c("chr", "start_hg19", "end_hg19")) |> mutate(Apert_fathersPanel = T)) |> 
  arrange(chr, start_hg19) |> 
  mutate(DD_fathersPanel = coalesce(DD_fathersPanel, FALSE),
    Apert_fathersPanel = coalesce(Apert_fathersPanel, FALSE))
  
write_tsv(SupTable7_TargetPanels, paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/SupTable7_TargetPanels.tsv"))

```

#### Combined xlsx
Run this to rewrite all to excel at once
```{r supTables}
supTables <- createWorkbook()

# Add each table as a new sheet
addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S1 Overview")
writeData(supTables, "Table S1 Overview", SupTable1_Overview)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S2 DNMs")
writeData(supTables, "Table S2 DNMs", SupTable2_DNMs)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S3 Trios")
writeData(supTables, "Table S3 Trios", SupTable3_Trios)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S4 DiagDNMs")
writeData(supTables, "Table S4 DiagDNMs", SupTable4_DiagDNMs)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S5 ClinicalReview")
writeData(supTables, "Table S5 ClinicalReview", SupTable5_ClinicalReview)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S6 SpermSamples")
writeData(supTables, "Table S6 SpermSamples", SupTable6_SpermSamples)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S7 TargetPanels")
writeData(supTables, "Table S7 TargetPanels", SupTable7_TargetPanels)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S8 SpermVars")
writeData(supTables, "Table S8 SpermVars", SupTable8_SpermVars)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S9 dNdSgeneLevel")
writeData(supTables, "Table S9 dNdSgeneLevel", SupTable9_dNdSgeneLevel)

addWorksheet(supTables, "Table S10 dNdShotspot")
writeData(supTables, "Table S10 dNdShotspot", SupTable10_dNdShotspot)

# Save the combined workbook
saveWorkbook(supTables, paste0(manuscriptPath, "Supplementary_Tables.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)

# Save each table as an individual xlsx file
write.xlsx(list("Table S1 Overview"       = SupTable1_Overview),       paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS1.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S2 DNMs"           = SupTable2_DNMs),           paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS2.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S3 Trios"          = SupTable3_Trios),          paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS3.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S4 DiagDNMs"       = SupTable4_DiagDNMs),       paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS4.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S5 ClinicalReview" = SupTable5_ClinicalReview), paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS5.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S6 SpermSamples"   = SupTable6_SpermSamples),   paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS6.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S7 TargetPanels"   = SupTable7_TargetPanels),   paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS7.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S8 SpermVars"      = SupTable8_SpermVars),      paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS8.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S9 dNdSgeneLevel"  = SupTable9_dNdSgeneLevel),  paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS9.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
write.xlsx(list("Table S10 dNdShotspot"   = SupTable10_dNdShotspot),   paste0(manuscriptPath, "SupTables/TableS10.xlsx"), overwrite = TRUE)
```
